messages:
Sam (Support): Hey team — Lee from ACME reports weird behaviour during a plan change at 2025-02-01T03:58:12Z: their monthly credits appear to have been moved early, API returned 429 for ~10m, then credits showed up doubled in the UI. Can someone explain what determines the exact refill/cutover timestamp?

Lee (ACME): @Sam yep. We upgraded their org from Starter -> Pro around 03:58 UTC. Expected pro-rata and immediate new bucket. Instead: 1) API started returning 429 for a few minutes on active streaming sessions, 2) UI showed zero, then after ~12m it showed the new Pro balance AND the old leftover tokens as a separate line (looked like duplication). No billing charge dup.

Sam (Support): Thanks. Can you paste the exact steps to reproduce or any request IDs?

Lee (ACME): Repro steps I gave customer:
- Keep a long streaming websocket open to streams.redwood.ai/v1/stream (conn stays alive)
- Start heavy token usage to drain Starter bucket down to small amount
- Trigger plan upgrade via dashboard at 03:58:12 UTC
- Observe: streaming clients got 429 and then resumed once UI refreshed.

Ivan (Backend): Possible hypothesis: we ran the billing_cutover job (billing_migration_2025_02) across partitions around that time. The migration writes a new tenant bucket key and nukes the old one, then triggers cache invalidation. If streaming checks token availability against a short-lived in-memory cache + Redis, there can be a race where Redis shows new bucket but cache still points to old (or vice versa). That explains a brief 429 window. The duplicated line in the UI suggests the old balance was retained in a migration log field rather than merged.

Elaine (Billing): TL;DR: pro-rata logic is based on billing cycle boundary + the plan_change timestamp (UTC). Pro-rate credit allocation should be computed server-side at plan change time. However, when a tenant is moved to the new billing bucket during a migration, we add a migration record (audit) with the leftover tokens. Normally we merge that into the new balance; if the merge job didn't run atomically you can see both. No customer was double-charged.

Josh (Platform): To add: streaming auth checks token availability by reading this sequence: in-memory token cache -> redis key credits:tenant:<id> -> fallback to billing service API. If the migration removed the redis key and created a new redis key name with a short TTL, some in-flight reads got a miss and the fallback returned 429 while the migration was still finalizing.

billing-bot: [billing_migration_2025_02] tenant=acme-tenant-1234 status=partial-migrate start=2025-02-01T03:56:08Z step=write-new-bucket

Ivan (Backend): Logs show migration started 03:56, write-new-bucket at 03:58:10, cache invalidation at 03:58:11, and merge-audit ran at 03:70:23 (typo: 04:10:23?) — merge-audit delayed by job queue congestion. That gap is your 10-12m window.

Sam (Support): OK actionable items: Ivan / Platform team — can you confirm: 1) why merge job was queued late, 2) whether we left tenant in inconsistent state, 3) if we can add a short circuit to avoid 429 for active streaming sessions during migration?

Ivan (Backend): I'll pull job runner traces and check queue backlog. Early note: our migration worker has a lower priority and was preempted by overnight maintenance for cluster-ops. Queue backpressure + a non-idempotent merge step caused the audit to be left as separate record.

Josh (Platform): Mitigation we can deploy: when migration writes new bucket, also write a temporary alias key with 1m TTL at the old key name that routes reads to new bucket until merge completes. That prevents misses for streaming reads. I can draft a hotfix today.

Elaine (Billing): For customer-facing explanation: we should tell them: 
- This was a migration race during billing cutover.
- No extra charge occurred.
- Credits were not lost; they appeared split due to a delayed merge.
- Short-term impact: transient 429 for in-flight streams.

Lee (ACME): Appreciate the investigation. Two asks from customer: 1) can you confirm no tokens were double-spent? 2) can you provide recommended client workaround (reconnect/backoff) to avoid 429 on plan changes?

Sam (Support): Elaine — can you confirm on billing side the double-spend check and sign off on a customer message?

Elaine (Billing): Confirmed: no double-billing. We will provide an email note: "migration race caused temporary split view of leftover and new credits; you were not charged twice."

Josh (Platform): Client workaround: advise streaming clients to handle a soft 429 by: 
1) pause + exponential backoff for 5-30s, then try lightweight status check: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/me/credits
2) if status returns new balance, resume streaming; if still 429, full reconnect.

Sam (Support): Next steps: Ivan to confirm root cause and timeline, Josh to prepare a config change (alias key + TTL) PR, Elaine to prepare customer-facing note. I'll draft a reply to ACME with steps and ETA.

Ivan (Backend): Assigned. I'll attach job traces and the redis operations in thread once I have them.

Sam (Support): Thanks — leaving this thread open until PR merged and customer note sent. :thumbsup:
